cases.purpose: Parity with util-linux write when the recipient is given as a user name: the user is looked up in the utmp login records and the message is delivered to that user's terminal, with the Message from banner, the text and the EOF marker.

files.mkutmp.py:
import struct, sys, time
line, user = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
# glibc/Linux struct utmp (384 bytes): type, pid, line[32], id[4], user[32], host[256], exit, session, tv(sec,usec), addr[4], unused[20]
rec = struct.pack('<hxxi32s4s32s256shhiii4i20s', 7, 4242, line.encode(), b'p1', user.encode(), b'', 0, 0, 0, int(time.time()), 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, b'')
assert len(rec) == 384, len(rec)
sys.stdout.buffer.write(rec)

cases.oracle: util-linux write(1) from bsdextrautils 2.41.5 on the reference PATH. A one-record Linux utmp file naming user u1 on the fixture PTY's own line is installed as /var/run/utmp by a root fixture in its private mount namespace; util-linux write selects the recipient terminal from that record. Screen contents decoded independently by pyte.
cases.comparison: Both builds run the same command, write u1, with the message on stdin. The reference delivers banner, text and EOF to the PTY and exits 0; the candidate (which takes a terminal path, not a user name) is compared with it on status, files and the same raw-byte expectations.
cases.reference_script:
t=$(/usr/bin/tty)
/usr/bin/python3 mkutmp.py "${t#/dev/}" u1 > /var/run/utmp
/usr/bin/chmod 664 /var/run/utmp
/usr/bin/chmod 620 "$t"
printf 'user-routed message\n' | { /usr/bin/find /usr /bin /sbin -name 'write*' -type f -perm -u+x > wfound 2>/dev/null; w=$(/usr/bin/head -n1 wfound); $w u1; }; echo "rc=$?" > rc
printf 'W-DONE\n'
cases.candidate_script:
t=$(/usr/bin/tty)
/usr/bin/python3 mkutmp.py "${t#/dev/}" u1 > /var/run/utmp
/usr/bin/chmod 664 /var/run/utmp
/usr/bin/chmod 620 "$t"
printf 'user-routed message\n' | write u1; echo "rc=$?" > rc
printf 'W-DONE\n'
